comments.author: unknown
comments.body:
⚠️ severity: IMPORTANT —
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: failure-analysis state is collected even while the feature is disabled**

`reconcileIssue` calls `collectFailureAnalysisState(...)` unconditionally:

```js
built.state.failureAnalysis = collectFailureAnalysisState(provider, issue.number, cfg.machineLogins);
```

With the feature off (missing `failureAnalysis` config → `{ enabled: false }` — the default for every existing consumer), this still performs **one `github_get_pr_comments` REST call per machine-managed issue per tick** (up to `issueLimit` = 50) and parses the full comment history — for gates that can never fire, since both `failureAnalysisGate` and `gateBlindRedispatch` check `failureAnalysisEnabledOf(cfg)` first and bail.

The PR's own invariant — "disabled/unreadable/unparseable leaves the loop byte-identical to today" — holds for *decisions* but not for *I/O*: this is a real API-quota/latency regression for every deployment that never opts in, and it also runs for issues the engine-skip (`blocked`/`needs-human`/active run) would immediately discard.

Suggested fix — gate it exactly like the sibling `blockedLabel` push in `action()`:

```js
built.state.failureAnalysis = (cfg.failureAnalysis && cfg.failureAnalysis.enabled)
    ? collectFailureAnalysisState(provider, issue.number, cfg.machineLogins)
    : null;
```

and pin it in the scripted replay: assert `issueComments` is never called while disabled (the scripted provider can record the fetches — the AC7 test already pins the label-query side of this).

comments.author: unknown
comments.body:
⚠️ severity: IMPORTANT —
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: the park can never re-engage — idempotency is keyed on the issue, not on the verdict episode**

The gate requires a **global** marker count of zero:

```js
if (verdict && verdict.classification === 'deterministic-infra' && faState.parkCommentCount === 0) {
```

`countParkComments` counts **all** `<!-- dmtools:failure-block ... -->` markers on the issue, across all history. Two permanent breakages follow:

1. **Second episode never parks (AC4 fallout).** After the first park episode, a human removes `sm:leg-blocked` (the documented resume gesture). If the failure returns — same signature after a failed human fix, or a brand-new failure mode — a fresh `deterministic-infra` verdict can never park again: the gate returns null (count is 1), the consumed `analyzedAtCount` suppresses re-analysis until the streak rebuilds, and once it does, the analyzer re-classifies deterministic-infra and is *ignored again*. The issue blind-retries forever while the analyzer keeps correctly screaming "deterministic". The code comment says the protection targets the **stale verdict of the cleared episode**; the implementation suppresses every future episode.

2. **A failed label-add strands the park half-applied.** `applyFailurePark` posts the comment first, then adds the label (deliberate order). If the label-add throws once (any REST hiccup), the next tick reads `parkCommentCount === 1` → gate null → the label is **never** retried — while the posted diagnostic claims "re-dispatch is STOPPED for this issue". Retries continue.

Fix direction: the park marker payload already carries `signature` — make the count signature-scoped, e.g. `countParkComments(comments, streakSignature)` counting only markers whose embedded signature matches the current streak signature. That keeps the intended AC4 protection (a stale same-signature verdict cannot re-park) while letting a genuinely new episode park, and a failed label-add re-enters the gate next tick. Please add a replay test: cleared park → new deterministic verdict for a *different* signature → expect label + exactly one new diagnostic.

comments.author: unknown
comments.body:
⚠️ severity: IMPORTANT —
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: park-marker counting is not machine-identity-gated (asymmetric trust vs the verdict markers)**

Verdict markers are parsed fail-closed against the machine-author allowlist (the gh-807 rule — `parseFailureVerdicts(..., { authorLogins })`), but `countParkComments` scans **every** comment body for the `dmtools:failure-block` marker regardless of author:

```js
function countParkComments(comments) {
    ...
    var start = body.indexOf(PARK_MARKER_PREFIX);
    if (start !== -1 && body.indexOf(PARK_MARKER_SUFFIX, start) !== -1) count++;
```

The marker format is public (it's in this repo), so any comment-capable identity — human or compromised leg — can post a one-line `<!-- dmtools:failure-block {} -->` and permanently hold `parkCommentCount ≥ 1`. Via the gate at `machineSmAgent.js:284` that silently suppresses **every future park action and diagnostic** on the issue: the forged marker doesn't park the issue (the doctrine holds) — it prevents the machine from parking it, fail-open, with no log trace. Every other machine-marker family in this codebase is fail-closed; this is the one write-adjacent counter that isn't.

Suggested fix: parse the marker payload and require a machine-authored author — e.g. route through `reviewVerdicts.parseMarkerComments` with the same `authorLogins` + `failClosed` discipline used for verdicts (the park marker JSON already exists, so a `parkMarkersFrom(comments, opts)` helper gives you both the count and the signature-scoping suggested in the sibling thread). Pin it with a forged-author test mirroring the "machine-identity gate" test in `test_failureAnalyzer.js`.

comments.author: unknown
comments.body:
💡 severity: SUGGESTION —
💡 **SUGGESTION: verdict free text lands unescaped in the park diagnostic's markdown**

The marker payload is marker-safe (`markerSafeReplacer` neutralizes `-->`/`<!--`), but the *rendered* body is raw markdown:

```js
(v.suspected_root_cause ? m.bold('Suspected root cause:') + ' ' + v.suspected_root_cause + '\n' : '') +
```

`suspected_root_cause` and `suggested_fix` originate from an AI analysis of raw CI logs; a crafted log line can smuggle headings, links or fences into a machine-authored comment (e.g. a "suggested fix" linking somewhere). `evidence` is fenced via `m.code`, but a log line containing ` ``` ` would break that fence too. GitHub neutralizes scripts, so impact is cosmetic/phishing at most — hence suggestion-tier — but the house rule elsewhere is that AI-derived text is data, not protocol.

Suggested fix: render the two free-text fields through `m.inline(...)`/`m.code(...)` (or escape markdown metacharacters), giving the diagnostic the same hygiene the marker payload already has.

comments.author: unknown
comments.body:
🪶 severity: NIT —
🪶 **NIT: "confidence null" renders in the park action reason**

When the verdict carries no confidence (`verdictFromPayload` defaults it to `null`), the audit reason becomes:

```
deterministic-infra verdict (confidence null) — parking: ...
```

Suggest omitting the parenthetical when `confidence` is null — the same degrade-to-omission rule the gh-1366 report applies to a missing phase ("no phase → no Phase line, never the literal string 'undefined'").

```js
'(' + (typeof verdict.confidence === 'number' ? 'confidence ' + verdict.confidence + ') ' : '') + ...
```
